facts.statement: The genus Kujdanowiaspis was first described by Stensiö in 1942.
Kujdanowiaspis lived during the Early Devonian period.
Fossils of Kujdanowiaspis have been found in Podolia (Ukraine), Poland, and Spain.
facts.quote: Kujdanowiaspis is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fish from the Early Devonian of Podolia (Ukraine), Poland and Spain.

facts.statement: The animal is known from numerous fragmentary head shields and body armours.
facts.quote: Kujdanowiaspis is known from many fragmentary head shields and body armours.

facts.statement: Three species were originally described for the genus in 1934: K. buczacziensis, K. podolica, and K. rectiformis.
facts.quote: Kujdanowiaspis consists of three species, all described in 1934: Kujdanowiaspis buczacziensis (type species), Kujdanowiapsis podolica, and Kujdanowiaspis rectiformis

facts.statement: A species named Kujdanowiaspis zychi in 1945 was later moved to the genus Erikaspis in 2007.
facts.quote: Kujdanowiaspis zychi was also named and described by Stensiö in 1945, but was reassigned to the new genus Erikaspis in 2007.

facts.statement: Kujdanowiaspis is considered one of the most basal members of the order Arthrodira.
facts.quote: Kujdanowiaspis is one of the more basal members of the order Arthrodira

facts.statement: The animal possessed a pronounced, serrated spinal plate that created a crescent-shaped dorsal silhouette.
facts.quote: It had a very pronounced, serrated spinal plate, giving it an almost lunate dorsal silhouette.

facts.statement: Its body shape and large lateral spinal plates suggest it lived a benthic lifestyle near the bottom of the water.
facts.quote: The body of Kujdanowiaspis is slightly wider than high, with large spinal plates protruding laterally, suggesting a benthic lifestyle.

facts.statement: Its underdeveloped jaws suggest it likely ate smaller, softer prey like mollusks or worms rather than tough animals.
facts.quote: Its jaws were comparatively underdeveloped in comparison to the more robust-jawed arthrodires that would come after it, such as Dunkleosteus and Coccosteus, indicating that it likely subsisted primarily on smaller, softer-bodied animals such as mollusks or worms instead of larger, tougher prey animals.

facts.statement: Kujdanowiaspis belongs to the family Kujdanowiaspididae.
Kujdanowiaspis is classified within the class Placodermi.
The genus lived between 419.62 and 410.62 million years ago, spanning the Lochkovian to Pragian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Lochkovian to Pragian (419.62 to 410.62 million years ago)
